pages.title: The Hot Big Bang
pages.text: $(thing)The Hot Big Bang$()$(br2)Everything we see was once hotter and denser than the inside of any star, and has been expanding and cooling ever since. The Friedmann equations of general relativity say how fast: by what fills the universe and how it is curved. The first study of the Origin.

$(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): General Relativity, Nucleosynthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Metric Tensor.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A homogeneous, isotropic universe is described by one scale factor a(t) that stretches every distance. Put such a space into general relativity: the square of the expansion rate H = (da/dt)/a is set by the density ρ of what fills it, by the curvature k of space, and by a vacuum energy Λ. Write the square of the expansion rate.
